issues.failure_explanation:
Two failures. (i) Every update in \cref{eq:msgfem:iteration} lies in $H^1_D(\domain)$: $\projB$ maps into $H^1_{D,0}(\osdomain_\ddindex)$ (zero on $(\osbdry\cap dryD)\cup(\osbdry\cap\domain)$), so $\pu_\ddindex\projB(\cdot)$ extended by zero vanishes on $ dryD$; and $\globalApproxSpace$ is spanned by $\pu_\ddindex\evecloc$ with $\evecloc\in H_B(\osdomain_\ddindex)\subseteq H^1_D(\osdomain_\ddindex)$, also vanishing on $ dryD$. Hence the $ dryD$-trace of $ wp^{(k)}$ is invariant under the iteration. For $ dryD
eq\emptyset$ and any $ wp^{(0)}\in\Hone$ whose trace mismatch $ wp^{(0)}|_{ dryD}- wpSol|_{ dryD}$ is non-constant, \cref{eq:msgfem:iteration:2} would force $
orm{ wp^{(k)}- wpSol}_{a,\domain}	o0$, which by Poincaré–Wirtinger and trace continuity is incompatible with a fixed non-constant trace mismatch; so the claimed convergence for any $ wp^{(0)}\in\Hone$ is false. (ii) The proof derives the operator bound $
orm{(I-\msgfemOperator) wpTest}\le\vartheta
orm{ wpTest}$ for all $ wpTest\in\Hone$ 'immediately' from \cref{eq:msgfem:iteration:1}, which is the bound at the single function $ wpSol$; extending it to all $ wpTest$ requires the full MS-GFEM error analysis for arbitrary data $ ilWF{ wpTest}{\cdot}{}$ plus a local stability estimate (and is impossible on all of $\Hone$ by (i)). issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the statement to initial guesses with correct Dirichlet trace ($\fwp^{(0)}-\fwpSol\in H^1_D(\domain)$, the natural class containing $0$ and $\fwpPart$), and prove contraction of $I-\msgfemOperator$ on $H^1_D(\domain)$ by running the error analysis for arbitrary data together with a local stability bound for $B$-harmonic extensions (cf. the repair of cor:added-1).

issues.title: Convergence theorem for the MS-GFEM iteration is false for general $H^1$ initial guesses and its proof gaps the operator-contraction step
issues.why_classification: A recognizably comparable result survives (contraction for correct-trace initial data, which covers all practically used starts and the discrete DG iteration), but the repair requires a quantifier restriction plus a contained nontrivial new argument, so it is more than minor and avoids major loss.

issues.failure_explanation: Let $\mat{M}_{RAS}=\sum_\ddindex\discRestriction\transpose\discPU\discBilForm_\ddindex^{-1}\discRestriction$ and $\mat{M}_c=\discCoarseRestriction\transpose\discBilForm_S^{-1}\discCoarseRestriction$. The matrix of $\projCoarse$ is $\discProjCoarse=\discBilForm_S^{-1}\discCoarseRestriction\discBilForm$ (the paper's own formula), i.e. $\mat{M}_c\discBilForm$, acting on the function remainder $w-Pw$; hence $\mat{\msgfemOperator}=\mat{M}_{RAS}\discBilForm+\mat{M}_c\discBilForm(\mat{I}-\mat{M}_{RAS}\discBilForm)=(\mat{M}_{RAS}+\mat{M}_c(\mat{I}-\discBilForm\,\mat{M}_{RAS}))\discBilForm$. The two-step scheme \cref{eq:discrete:RAS} applies the coarse solve to the updated residual $\vec{\rhsF}-\discBilForm\vec{\fwp}^{(k+1/2)}=(\mat{I}-\discBilForm\mat{M}_{RAS})\vec{r}_k$, i.e. it is Richardson with $\mat{M}_{RAS}+\mat{M}_c(\mat{I}-\discBilForm\mat{M}_{RAS})$. The defined $\discPreconditioner$ instead contains $(\mat{I}-\mat{M}_{RAS})$; it equals the correct factor only if $\mat{M}_c(\discBilForm-\mat{I})\mat{M}_{RAS}=0$, which fails in general. Thus $\mat{\msgfemOperator}=\discPreconditioner\discBilForm$ is false and \cref{eq:msgfem:iteration:discrete} with this $\discPreconditioner$ is not equivalent to \cref{eq:discrete:RAS}; as printed, $\discPreconditioner$ defines a different, primal/dual-incoherent preconditioner (it subtracts a function update from a residual before the coarse solve).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We choose the rotating velocity field

issues.failure_explanation: For the stated field, $\divergence\velField=\partial_1\velField_1+\partial_2\velField_2=-80(x_1-0.5)(x_2-0.5)-3$, which is positive on a set of positive measure (about $+17$ near $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$; positive wherever $(x_1-0.5)(x_2-0.5)<-3/80$) and about $-23$ near $(0,0)$ and $(1,1)$; only its mean is negative ($-3$). So the field has mixed-sign divergence, not negative divergence. (Its linearization near the center is also saddle-type, with eigen-directions $(1,1)$ and $(1,-1)$, so calling it 'rotating' is inaccurate as well.) The problem is nevertheless indefinite because $\divergence\velField$ reaches large negative values with $\diffMin=10^{-6}$, so the conclusion survives while the stated reason is false.
